To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the dorsal stream is dependent on visual form information, and that this dependence is mediated by inputs from the ventral stream, which are necessary for the flexible control of action.

(i) the ventral visual stream is crucial for the guidance of visually guided actions, and (ii) the dorsal visual stream is crucial in certain aspects of perceptual function in both ventral and dorsal streams.

(i) the dorsal visual stream can be functionally dissociated from the ventral stream in a patient with visual agnosia, and (ii) the dorsal visual pathway can be functionally reactivated by the ventral visual pathway in a patient with a parietal stroke.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the nature and significance of interactions between visual systems in the two streams, and how these interactions might contribute to human visual function.
how the two visual streams work together to mediate visual function, and how this is achieved in the normal brain, as well as in the brain after injury.
understanding the functional architecture of the primate cerebral cortex, and the ways in which it is organized to support perception, action and cognition.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the two streams are not independent, but interact with each other at various levels of processing.
there are no hard and fast divisions between the two visual streams.
the dorsal and ventral visual streams are not functionally independent, but that each has a unique contribution to make to the overall visual system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the dorsal stream is not a mere conduit for the ventral stream’s products, but rather that the two systems are highly interdependent.

both streams have a crucial role to play in the control of visuomotor function, with the posterior dorsal stream providing a direct route for the visual guidance of movement, and the ventral stream providing an indirect route, via its role in perceptual function.
the dorsal stream is not as isolated as was once thought, and is in fact highly dependent on the ventral stream for certain types of visual information.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, although the ventral stream has a clear and important role in mediating visuomotor control, this role is limited to a subset of the visuomotor tasks in which the parietal cortex is known to play a role.
the two streams do indeed have different functions but they are far from independent.
the two streams are more closely integrated than is often assumed, and that they can each make important contributions to the other’s function.
